note: D1 against the exam creator's un-blind grade as the expert reference (as D2 uses the exam author). Aggregates only. Generated by scripts/analysis/cslaw_creator_reference.py.

definitions.reference: the creator's grade (one per answer, raw 0-100). The creator wrote the case and the model solution and graded un-blind (benchmark role 'creator').
definitions.subsets: human_written = the 30 annotation answers (classic and co-creation), the paper's agreement basis; all = the 45 answers incl. the 15 model-generated ones
definitions.totals: sheet arms (zero-shot, few-shot) use the step sum 100 * sum(clip(score, 0, max)) / sum(max) as in cslaw_first_iteration_local.py; holistic arms use the stored total (dimension sum)
definitions.per_pass: mae, bias (judge - reference) and Pearson r are computed per pass and averaged over the complete passes (passes with a total on every answer of the subset), as in compute_d2_validity.py; first_pass = per answer the lowest run index present
definitions.vs_blind_mean / vs_pool4: the same statistics against the mean of the three blind grades and against the mean of all four grades (the paper's pool)
definitions.human_baseline: each blind grader against the creator on the answers they graded; pair_level = mean over all blind grades of |blind - creator| (each answer has three), the counterpart of one judge pass; grader_level_mean_mae = unweighted mean of the per-grader MAEs; blind_mean_vs_creator = the mean of three blind grades
definitions.alt_test_creator: Calderon et al. (ACL 2025) alternative-annotator test, single-expert variant (section D.2) with the creator as the expert, run with the benchmark's compute_agreement._alt_test_single_expert: per blind annotator j, instance wins by point-wise distance to the creator (ties count for both), d = W_h - W_f, one-sided test of d_bar < epsilon (t for n_j >= 30, else exact Wilcoxon), Benjamini-Yekutieli FDR at q .05, annotators with n_j < 5 dropped, winning rate omega = rejected / m, pass iff omega >= 0.5. epsilon 0.2 (the benchmark's headline), 0.15 as sensitivity. Run on the first pass and on each complete pass; per_annotator detail for the first pass on the human-written subset
definitions.cloud_ratio: MAE against the blind mean divided by half the mean within-answer max-min spread of the three blind grades. benchmark_definition: numerator first pass on the 30 human-written answers, spread over all 45 answers (the benchmark's 10.83 / 11.94 = 0.91); pass_mean: numerator averaged over complete passes; matched_30: spread over the same 30 answers; all_45: numerator on all 45 answers
definitions.paired: sheet arm minus the same judge's holistic arm in per-answer absolute error; pass_mean = per answer the mean over each arm's complete passes (compute_d2_validity Cell.abs_err), first_pass = first pass only; exam-cluster bootstrap (15 exams resampled with replacement, seed 20260806, 10000 draws, percentile 95 % CI); negative = the sheet is closer

caveats: The creator graded un-blind: they wrote the case and the model solution and knew both while grading.
The creator graded with the same 10-dimension scheme the holistic instrument uses, so the holistic arms share the reference's grading frame.
The generated sheets (zero-shot and few-shot) are built from the same model solution the creator wrote, so the sheet arms and the reference draw on one source.
4 creators cover the 15 exams. The reference is one grade per answer, so creator and exam effects are confounded and the reference carries no measured repeat noise.
2 of the 5 blind graders created other exams; no blind grade comes from the exam's own creator.
The alt-test has m = 5 blind annotators with 14 to 21 answers each on the 30 human-written answers, so omega moves in steps of 1/m and its Clopper-Pearson CI is wide.

notes.control_primary_rows_differ_from_export: control_results_temp0.jsonl carries a different single-pass total for the benchmark's primary judge than the benchmark's export on 1 of 45 answers; this script takes the export (the benchmark's own loader)
